sections.html:
New Haven sits on its harbor on the north shore of Long Island Sound, in the South Central Connecticut Planning Region. It was settled in 1638 and incorporated as a city in 1784. The city covers 20.14 square miles, and the 2020 census counted 134,023 people, which ranks it third among Connecticut cities. The count has climbed with every census since 2000, but a growing city does not by itself set what any single house will bring.

Yale University is the largest employer and the largest taxpayer, with Yale New Haven Hospital close behind. Because a few big institutions carry so much of the local economy, a local agent can tell you how they shape demand near your street.

The name on your address changes how a buyer pictures a house. Downtown centers on the Green, and the rest of the city is usually described by compass direction.

  • West and west central: Dixwell, Dwight, Beaver Hills, Edgewood, West River, Westville, Amity and West Rock-Westhills.
  • South: The Hill, City Point (also called Oyster Point) and the harborside Long Wharf district.
  • North: East Rock, Cedar Hill, Prospect Hill and Newhallville.
  • East: Mill River, Wooster Square, Fair Haven, Quinnipiac Meadows and Fair Haven Heights.
  • Harbor east side: The Annex and East Shore, also known as Morris Cove.

Wooster Square is an Italian-American neighborhood. Fair Haven lies between the Mill and Quinnipiac rivers, and its Quinnipiac River Historic District is one of dozens in the city. Inside a historic district? Ask the city before planning any exterior work.

Parts of the city are low and close to the water. Tropical storms have reached New Haven before, including the 1938 Hurricane, Carol in 1954 and Gloria in 1985. Your insurer and your attorney can tell you the flood status of a specific lot, and a buyer's lender is likely to ask the same thing.

The city is also known as The Elm City for its early tree-planting program, so mature trees are part of many yards. Look at large limbs and roots near the roofline and the sewer line before a buyer's inspector does.

sections.h2: How New Haven bills real estate tax
sections.html:
The fiscal year runs July 1 to June 30, and tax is billed in advance. The July 1 payment pays for July 1 through December 31. The January 1 payment pays for January 1 through June 30. One bill covers both and usually arrives in June.

After a closing, the buyer owes the next bill that comes due, whether that is July 1 or January 1. Any adjustment between you and the buyer is written into the contract, so refer closing questions to your attorney.

  • Office of the Tax Collector, 165 Church Street, first floor, New Haven, CT 06510. Open Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.
  • In person: cash, check, money order or bank check. The office does not take cards.
  • By mail: Collector of Taxes, City of New Haven, P.O. Box 1927, New Haven, CT 06509-1927. Put your tax account number on the payment.
  • Online: debit cards carry a $3.25 fee, credit cards 2.5 percent, and ACH payments a 0.75 fee with a five business day hold.

Ask the Tax Collector for a payoff figure good through your closing date.

sections.h2: Conveyance tax on a New Haven sale
sections.html:
Any deed at $2,000 or above is taxable. Filing waits at the clerk's counter until the return and the payment are both in hand.

  • Connecticut's cut on a residential sale begins at 0.75 percent of the first $800,000, moves to 1.25 percent between $800,000.01 and $2,500,000, and reaches 2.25 percent beyond.
  • New Haven's cut is 0.25 percent of the full price.
  • An owner-occupied house with a certified pyrrhotite foundation may be exempt, but only on its first sale after certification.

A targeted investment community may add up to one-fourth of one percent more. Your contract and closing attorney decide which side pays.

Most owners compare a listing with a fast cash sale. Three things decide it: the shape the house is in, the neighborhood, and how soon you need to close.

  • Listing: more potential buyers, along with showings, financing contingencies and repair haggling.
  • Cash buyer: the house goes as-is, there is no lender, and you and the title company agree on the date.
  • Investor who will rent or renovate: faster, normally at a price reflecting the work ahead.

Triggers vary. Some people inherit a house, some own a property with tenants, some carry back taxes, and some face deferred repairs. We review each situation and give a written offer with no obligation. We do not promise a price, and the final number depends on what we find.

A house with tenants can be sold with the tenants in place, and a cash buyer can take it that way. Their lease still binds the new owner, and local rules still apply, so read the lease before you talk to anyone and have an attorney confirm the details. Tell the buyer up front about the rent, the deposit and any unit you are not allowed to enter without notice. Surprises about occupancy are the quickest way to lose trust in a sale.

sections.h2: Before you hand over the keys
sections.html:
A few small jobs prevent delays. Cancel or transfer utilities for the day of closing, and take final meter readings if you can. Collect warranties and manuals for anything that stays. Photograph the empty house as a record of its condition. If you have a homeowner's policy, keep it active until the deed is recorded, then cancel it and ask about a refund of any unused premium.

Forward your mail through the post office, and update the address on your driver's license, bank and insurer. None of this is complicated, but doing it in one sitting beats finding out later that a bill is still going to the old house.

sections.h2: What happens after you say yes
sections.html:
1. The title company or attorney opens the file and searches the title.
  2. You request a payoff letter from any mortgage lender, and the Tax Collector provides the tax figure.
  3. You sign the deed and the conveyance tax return is filed with the town clerk.
  4. Taxes, liens and your loan are paid from the proceeds, and you receive the rest.

Bring government ID and your most recent mortgage and tax statements. Move your belongings out before closing, and leave keys, remotes and any manuals for the new owner. With a cash purchase there is no lender's appraisal or loan approval standing between you and the signing, which is why the date is easier to control.

faqs.q: How many people live in New Haven, CT?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 134,023, and the 2025 estimate is 138,774. Only two Connecticut cities are larger.

faqs.q: When are New Haven property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first payment is due July 1 and covers July 1 to December 31. The second is due January 1 and covers January 1 to June 30. The city mails a single bill, usually in June.

faqs.q: Who pays the next tax bill after a New Haven closing?
faqs.a: Whoever buys the house owes the next installment to come due, July 1 or January 1. Any adjustment goes into the contract through your closing attorney.

faqs.q: Where do I pay New Haven taxes in person?
faqs.a: At the Office of the Tax Collector, 165 Church Street, first floor, weekdays 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. It accepts cash, check, money order or bank check, but not cards.

faqs.q: What conveyance tax will a New Haven seller face?
faqs.a: For a house under $800,000 the base rate totals 1 percent, with 0.75 going to the state and 0.25 to the city. Above that the state's rate climbs to 1.25 percent, then 2.25 percent.
